lines.text: seek some power which rules the world according to your
desires, your understanding, and your ideals, but to seek the
Creator who rules the world according to His own inscrutable
will. If you are seeking God you are seeking the Lord and
Ruler of the world, whom you will only know when you
are ready to recognize yourself as His creature, when you are
ready to allow Him to be God, and to surrender yourself
unreservedly to His will, even though His being is utterly
incomprehensible to you and wrapped in darkness. Luther
says: "Whoever refuses to suffer, can know no God as
Creator, for such a one is not prepared to be nothing, that
God might be his Creator." "It is the way of God first of all
to destroy and humble to the dust what is in us, before He
bestows on us the gift of His grace." Whoever resists this
destruction "as by fire"
, to him God the Creator becomes an
adverse destructive fate, and the countenance of God
changes for such a one into the countenance of the devil.
God is our Creator; and all laments and accusations, all
doubts and all despair, arise from the fact that the true idea
of God has become lost to us and, ever anew, threatens to
be dissolved. And this basic sin of denying God as Creator
and asserting one's own right to life is working out its
terrible consequences in every department of life; it is like a
poison which is ruining both the life of the individual and
of the community. From the fact that men assert and insist
on their right, that they first and foremost make their claims
to life instead of asking what is required of them, there
arises envy and hatred, contempt for the laws of nature which
sustain life, strife and distress both on a small and a big scale.
No man who exists is without wishes and longings, and no
living man can be, any more than a child can have no
desires in its relations with its parents. But just as it never
enters the head of a true child to suppose that it must make
claims on its parents and that it has a right to their kindness,
just as the child waits confidently for the fulfilment of its
desires as a sheer gift, so we adults must not presumptuously
assert our right to a good life. We must rather be prepared
